title: Food standards: amendment of standards of identity for enriched grain products to require addition of folic acid
journal: Federal Register 61(44): 8781-8797, final rule, Docket No. 91N-100S, 5 March 1996
result: Requires folic acid in enriched cereal-grain products at 140 µg per 100 g (0.635 mg/lb), effective 1 January 1998, to help women of childbearing age meet the 1992 Public Health Service recommendation of 0.4 mg daily; the PHS also advised keeping total folate below 1 mg/day except under medical supervision because high intakes mask the anaemia of B12 deficiency while neurological damage progresses. FDA modelled 70, 140 and 350 µg per 100 g with 1987-1988 USDA consumption data: adding fruit juices and dairy products pushed some non-target groups above 1 mg/day even at the lowest level; 350 µg per 100 g gave intakes up to 1220 µg/day. With 140 µg per 100 g, breakfast cereals up to 100 µg per serving and supplements up to 400 µg, 95th-percentile intakes of adults aged 51 years and over could reach 840 to 860 µg/day, a level FDA recognised as approaching the safe upper limit without accounting for under-reporting of food intake.
